plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 10: Fixed-Axis Rotation
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of the torque produced by a force acting at a point away from the origin. Thin black axes labeled x toward the lower left, y to the right, and z upward meet at a point marked O. A heavy blue arrow labeled r, with an overhead vector arrow, runs from O down and to the right to a black dot labeled P. At P a red arrow labeled F points to the right and slightly upward, and a dashed line extends the line of r past P; the angle between that dashed extension and F is marked theta, with the same angle theta repeated on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues to the lower right. A thin segment from near the origin meets that dashed line at a small right-angle square and is labeled r_perp. An orange arrow labeled tau rises straight up from P, standing perpendicular to the plane that holds r and F. Below and to the left, a drawn open right hand repeats the same blue r and red F arrows with curved black arrows wrapping around them to indicate the sense in which the fingers curl. Showing the geometric construction and the hand together supplies both the magnitude of the cross product, fixed by r, F, and theta, and its direction, which here lies along the positive z-axis.

elements: x, y, and z axes lines emerging from origin O
position vector r (thick blue arrow) from O to point P
point P (black dot)
force vector F (thick red arrow) originating at P
torque vector tau (thick orange arrow) originating at P, pointing strictly upwards
dashed line extending the direction of r past P
dashed line representing the backward line of action of F
angle arc theta between extended r and F
lever arm r_perp (thin black line) from origin intersecting F's line of action
right-angle square marker at the intersection of r_perp and the line of action
right-hand rule visualization (stylized 3D curved arrows wrapping from r toward F, with an optional hand sprite)
text labels: O, P, x, y, z, r, F, tau, theta, r_perp

interactions.teaches: Spatial relationships: r and F lie in the same flat plane, while the resulting torque tau is strictly perpendicular to that entire plane.

interactions.label: Angle θ
interactions.teaches: As the angle between r and F approaches 90°, the lever arm r_perp and the torque magnitude maximize; at 0° or 180° (parallel vectors), torque vanishes.

interactions.label: Overlay
interactions.teaches: The geometric view proves the torque magnitude |tau| = r * F * sin(θ) via the lever arm, while the right-hand rule demonstrates the cross-product direction.

demo_steps.title: Small angle, small torque
demo_steps.narration: At a small angle θ, the force is nearly parallel to r. The perpendicular lever arm r_perp is short, resulting in a small torque vector τ.

demo_steps.title: Maximum torque at 90°
demo_steps.narration: When F is perpendicular to r (θ = 90°), the lever arm extends to the full length of r. This maximizes the resulting torque magnitude.

demo_steps.title: Direction via Right-Hand Rule
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the right-hand rule cue. Curling fingers from r toward F shows how the right hand's thumb naturally points along the positive z-axis, parallel to τ.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Origin O at (0,0,0). Axes span ~6 units (X out-left, Y right, Z up). Position r lies in the xy-plane: P = (4, 3, 0), length |r| = 5. Force F originates at P, lies in the xy-plane, length |F| = 4. F's direction is the direction of r rotated around Z by angle theta. Torque tau = r × F, originating at P; since both are in xy-plane, tau is purely in the z-direction with magnitude |r||F|sin(theta). Scale tau's visual length by 0.25 to fit nicely. Lever arm r_perp connects origin to F's line of action at point P_proj = P - (P·F_hat)F_hat. Colors: r blue #255885, F red #ce4248, tau orange #e78f35. The Right-Hand Rule visual should only show when its toggle is active, hiding r_perp and the dashed lines.
interactionPlan.notes: Reactively update all geometries when theta changes: F vector rotates, tau scales, r_perp projection point moves, and angle arc updates. The angle arc theta is drawn between the normalized vector of r and F at P. In the 'Right-Hand Rule' mode, render curved 3D arrows spanning the angle from r to F around the z-axis at P to represent the curl of the fingers.

When a force F→ is applied to a point P whose position is r→ relative to O (the figure), the torque τ→ around O is

The cross product r→×F→ also tells us the sign of the torque. In the figure, the cross product r→×F→ is along the positive z-axis, which by convention is a positive torque. If r→×F→ is along the negative z-axis, this produces a negative torque.

Now let’s consider how to define torques in the general three-dimensional case.

The torque is perpendicular to the plane defined by r→andF→ and its direction is determined by the right-hand rule.

Figure shows an XYZ coordinate system. Force F is applied in the XY plane and is parallel to the X axis. Vector r lies in the XY plane. It starts at the origin of the origin of the coordinate system and ends at the beginning of vector F. Vector for torque starts at the intersection point of r and v vectors. It is perpendicular to the XY plane and is pointed into the Z direction.

Implement a 2D sprite or 3D model for the hand to explicitly illustrate the right-hand rule, rather than using abstract curved lines.
